Sydney's warehouse belt

Event Planners in Inner West

An empty warehouse is the Inner West signature venue, and it is also the hardest kind of room to plan. Power, catering, bathrooms and every stick of furniture arrive on a truck. Send one brief and hear from planners who already have the supplier list that job needs.

The room is cheap. Everything that makes it a venue is not.

A bare warehouse looks like a bargain until you price power, bathrooms, a kitchen, furniture, lighting and a bump in that starts the day before. Planners here quote that honestly.

Inner West Council covers Sydney's old industrial belt, and that history is why the area's event spaces look nothing like the rest of the city. Former factories and workshops in Marrickville, St Peters, Rozelle and Sydenham now hire out as blank rooms: brick, concrete, high ceilings, a roller door and very little else. Good event planners in Inner West Sydney are judged on their supplier list, because a bare space needs hire, power, kitchen access, lighting and often bathrooms brought in before it becomes a venue at all.

The rest of the area behaves differently again. Balmain, Rozelle and Birchgrove sit on a peninsula of narrow terrace streets. Newtown, Enmore and Petersham carry the live music and small bar trade. Ashfield, Summer Hill and Dulwich Hill run along the inner west rail line with the halls and clubs that come with it.

In and around Inner West

What are you planning in Inner West?

Six kinds of brief come out of this area, and the venue type usually decides how hard each one is. A licensed room is straightforward. A warehouse is a build.

Start with

Weddings

Warehouse weddings are the local speciality, and they are a construction job with a guest list attached. Everything comes in: catering kitchen, bar, furniture, lighting, sometimes bathrooms and a generator. A planner who has built one in Marrickville or Rozelle already knows which hire companies can access the loading bay.

Find planners

Parties and milestones

Thirtieths and fortieths here tend to book a bar upstairs room or a converted space off King Street, then run late. The two things to settle early are the noise condition on the venue's licence and how a hundred people leave a terrace street at midnight without waking it.

Find planners

Corporate events

Creative studios, breweries, tech offices and the university and hospital campuses nearby all run events in this area, and they want the warehouse look rather than a hotel ballroom. Product launches, film and music industry nights and staff parties are the common briefs, usually with heavy AV.

Find planners

Engagement parties

A backyard in Haberfield or Summer Hill, eighty people and a caterer is a very Inner West engagement party. It looks casual and it is not: a marquee on a terrace lawn needs measuring, the neighbours need warning, and a wet weather plan needs somewhere real to go.

Find planners

Proposals

The Bay Run, the Balmain and Birchgrove foreshore and the parklands at Sydney Park give this area its proposal spots, all of them public and all of them busy on a Saturday morning. A planner handles the permit, the timing and the friend positioned with a camera.

Find planners

Private celebrations

Naming days, wakes, book launches, exhibition openings and community fundraisers run constantly through the halls and converted spaces here, often on a small budget and a short timeline. Coordination rather than full planning usually fits, with the planner brought in for the last month.

Planning support

How much help do you want in Inner West?

Choose the level of help by counting what has to be brought in. A licensed venue with its own kitchen and staff needs a coordinator. A bare warehouse with a generator and hired bathrooms needs someone across it for months.

Full planning

A planner carries the whole build with you, from the first budget conversation to the last supplier leaving.

Usually engaged nine to fourteen months out.

  • Venue and supplier shortlists
  • Contracts and payment schedule
  • Run sheet and floor plan
  • On the day, start to finish

Partial planning

You have made a start. A planner picks up the parts that have stalled and brings the rest into one plan.

Often engaged four to eight months out.

On-the-day coordination

Your plan is built. A coordinator takes it over in the final weeks and runs the day so you can be in it.

Usually engaged four to eight weeks out.

  • Reads and stress-tests your plan
  • Confirms every supplier
  • Owns the run sheet
  • First point of contact on the day

Venue sourcing

Planners who know a market can shortlist against your date, your numbers and your budget rather than sending you back to the same search results.

Event coordination

Coordination is the execution layer: suppliers confirmed, a run sheet everyone has, and one person answering questions on the day.

Wedding coordination

A wedding coordinator takes a plan you have already built and runs the day itself, so nobody in the wedding party is directing traffic.

Choosing well

Finding the right planner in Inner West

The right questions here are all about what the venue does not include. Four of them will tell you quickly whether a planner has worked in a raw space before.

No. 01

Ask for their bare venue checklist

Anyone who has run a warehouse event has a list, and it is long: power supply and distribution, a kitchen or a catering tent, refrigeration, bathrooms, waste, cleaning, furniture, bar equipment, lighting, heating, signage and a wet weather plan for the queue outside. Ask to see it. A planner who cannot produce one has not built an event from nothing.

No. 02

Ask how the truck gets to the door

Load in is the quiet killer in this area. Most terrace streets have no truck parking, some warehouse loading bays open onto a lane that a semi cannot turn into, and several buildings share access with a business that trades on Saturday. Ask who has walked the route, what size vehicle fits, and whether a road occupancy permit is needed.

No. 03

Check the noise condition, not the closing time

A venue's licensed closing time and its noise condition are different numbers, and the second one is what stops the music. Development consents on converted industrial buildings in residential streets often cap amplified sound well before the bar closes. Get the actual condition in writing and design the run sheet around it, including where the speeches sit.

No. 04

Ask about aircraft if you are outdoors

Marrickville, Tempe, St Peters and Sydenham sit under the Sydney Airport approach, and the noise is regular rather than occasional. It will not ruin a party. It will ruin an outdoor speech or an unmiked ceremony. A planner who works this pocket will know the curfew hours and will put the vows and the toasts where the sky is quiet.

A warehouse is not a venue. It is a shell, and someone has to build the venue inside it.

On the ground

What it actually takes to fill an empty warehouse

Three constraints define event work across Inner West Council: rooms that arrive with nothing in them, streets that were never built for trucks, and a flight path over the southern suburbs.

The empty room is the whole job

Hire is the largest single line in a warehouse budget, and it is easy to underestimate by half. A bare space typically needs power distribution or a generator, a catering tent or kitchen hire, refrigeration, portable bathrooms if the building's are inadequate, tables, chairs, linen, glassware, bar fridges, lighting rig, heating in winter and a cleaning crew afterwards. It also needs time. A build like that usually wants access from the day before, which means paying for two days of venue hire rather than one, and the quote should say so.

Terrace streets and the peninsula

Balmain, Rozelle, Birchgrove and Annandale sit on narrow streets laid out before cars, and Balmain in particular is a peninsula with limited ways on and off. That affects three things: where a truck can stand, where guests park, and how long a supplier takes to get in and out. Suppliers sometimes price Balmain differently for that reason. If your event is on the peninsula, ask early whether the hire quote assumes a long carry from the nearest legal parking spot.

Sound, from above and from the street

Two noise problems run in opposite directions here, and both belong on the run sheet.

  • Aircraft: Marrickville, Tempe, St Peters and Sydenham sit under the Sydney Airport approach, so outdoor speeches need amplification or a gap in the schedule.
  • Neighbours: converted buildings in residential streets carry noise conditions that stop amplified music earlier than the licence closes.
  • Departure: a hundred guests leaving a terrace street at midnight is the complaint that ends a venue's goodwill, so plan a quiet exit and book transport to a single pick up point.

Questions

Planning an event in Inner West

What does a planner cost for an Inner West warehouse event?

Expect the planning fee to be quoted on scope rather than venue, but expect the total event budget to sit higher than a comparable event in a serviced venue. A bare space shifts cost from the venue line to the hire line, and the hire line is where the money goes: power, kitchen, bathrooms, furniture, lighting and two days of access instead of one. Ask any planner to quote the build separately from their fee.

Is a warehouse wedding harder to plan than a venue wedding?

Yes, substantially, and the difference is about six weeks of extra work. A serviced venue supplies a kitchen, staff, furniture, bathrooms, licences and a floor plan that already works. A warehouse supplies four walls and a roller door. Everything else is sourced, delivered, installed, run and removed, usually across a two day access window. That is why couples booking a raw space in Marrickville or Rozelle engage a planner earlier than they otherwise would.

Does aircraft noise really affect an event in Marrickville?

It affects outdoor talking, not indoor dancing. Marrickville, Tempe, St Peters and Sydenham sit under the Sydney Airport approach, so an unamplified ceremony or a speech on a rooftop will be interrupted at intervals during the day. Inside a brick warehouse with the doors shut it is a non issue. If your ceremony is outdoors, use a microphone, and ask your planner to schedule the vows and the toasts with that in mind.

How do guests get to an Inner West venue?

By train, mostly, and the Metro made the southern end easier. Sydenham is a Metro station as well as a suburban one, Newtown, Stanmore, Petersham, Lewisham, Summer Hill and Ashfield sit on the inner west line, and Dulwich Hill is served by the light rail from Central. Balmain, Rozelle and Birchgrove have no station at all, so plan buses, a ferry or a shuttle if your venue is on the peninsula.

Can I have a party in my Inner West backyard?

Usually yes, with three things sorted first. Measure the yard properly, because a marquee that fits on paper often does not clear a terrace fence line or a Hills hoist. Tell the neighbours, since houses here share walls and fences and a complaint at 10pm ends the night. Then plan the bathroom question honestly: eighty guests through one household bathroom for five hours is the detail that turns a good party bad.

Will a planner source the venue as well as run the event?

Most will, and in this area it is worth paying for. Raw spaces in Marrickville, St Peters, Rozelle and Lilyfield are not all listed as venues, some are studios or workshops that hire out occasionally, and availability moves. A planner who works the area knows which buildings take events, what each one allows, and which ones have a loading bay that fits a truck. Ask whether venue sourcing sits inside the fee or beside it.
